conversation.content:
Good morning—thank you for coming in today. I’m Dr. Ramirez, a perinatal mental-health clinician. My role is simply to listen and help you feel supported as you navigate these first weeks with your new baby.

I’d like to do a quick check-in using the EPDS—the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale. It’s a 10-question tool that looks at how you’ve been feeling emotionally over the past seven days. It’s not a test of your parenting; it’s just a way to see how we can best support you right now.

Everything you share stays between us unless you or your baby’s safety is at immediate risk. We’ll go at your pace, and you can pause any time.

Ready to begin? Thinking about the past week: overall, have you been able to enjoy things as much as you usually do, or has that been difficult for you?

Honestly… not really. I still smile when my little guy coos, but even the things I used to like—watching my shows, going for coffee—feel kind of flat. I’ll do them more because I hope they’ll help, but the spark isn’t there.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Sometimes I can laugh—like when my husband sends me those silly memes—but it feels forced, and it doesn’t last. Most of the time the funny side just seems far away.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not much. I’ll make plans—like meeting a friend for a walk or ordering my favorite take-out—but when the time comes, I feel “meh” and would rather stay on the couch. It’s like the excitement never shows up.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah... a lot. If the baby’s fussy, I immediately think it’s because I’m doing something wrong—maybe my milk isn’t good enough or I’m not holding him the “right” way. Even little stuff, like dropping a burp cloth, turns into “I’m such a failure at this mom thing.” I know in my head it’s not rational, but the guilt just pops up.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding him and suddenly worry his breathing sounds different, or I’ll lie in bed imagining the bassinet tipping over—things that haven’t happened and probably won’t. I know it’s “for no good reason,” but the thoughts just barge in and it takes me a while to talk myself down.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

A few times this week. Once, I was just folding laundry and my heart started racing and I felt shaky, like something awful was about to happen, even though nothing was wrong. It passed after a few minutes, but it left me feeling on-edge the rest of the evening.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes. Most days feel like I’m barely treading water—dishes pile up, the baby needs me, texts go unanswered, and I just want to hide. I still get everything done, but it’s like I’m moving through quicksand, and sometimes I end up crying in the nursery because it all feels like too much.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah. I lie down exhausted, but my brain won’t shut off—keeps replaying every little thing I think I did wrong that day or imagining scary what-ifs about the baby. I finally drift off, then wake up an hour or two later with my heart pounding. It’s been like that three, maybe four nights this week.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty often. I’d say most days this week I’ve just felt this heavy sadness sitting on me. It’s not tears every second, but it’s like the color’s drained out of everything and I can’t shake the gloom.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… I’ve cried a couple of times. Once was after a night when the baby wouldn’t settle and I felt like I was failing him. The other time was when my mom offered to help and I just felt this wave of guilt—like I should be able to handle everything myself.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

I’ve had a couple of quick flashes—like wondering if I just disappeared, would everyone be better off—but I haven’t made any plans or wanted to act on it. They’re scary thoughts, and I push them away, but they’ve popped into my head once or twice this week.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note (self-report)

Affect:
- Predominantly low mood ("heavy sadness," color drained)
- Anhedonia (minimal anticipatory or in-the-moment pleasure)

Cognitive:
- Excessive self-blame/guilt ("failure at this mom thing")
- Intrusive catastrophic worries about infant safety
- Fleeting passive self-harm ideation ("if I disappeared...") without intent or plan

Physical/Behavioral:
- Initial and middle insomnia linked to rumination and anxiety
- Episodic panic-like symptoms (heart racing, shaking)
- Daily tasks completed but with significant effort ("quicksand")
- Tearfulness when feeling inadequate or offered help

Coping/Support:
- Feels "on-edge," "meh," "overwhelmed" most days
- Uses distraction (memes) and cognitive self-talk with limited relief

Screening significance:
- Meets provisional cutoff indicators for moderate-to-severe postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety
- Safety factor: passive suicidal cognitions present; no active plan → requires further risk assessment

Recommend EDINBURGH POSTNATAL DEPRESSION SCALE completion and prompt follow-up with OB/MH provider for comprehensive evaluation, support resources, and safety planning.
